Across iterations 0 to 3, max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 m whatever the gains. Raising ki (iteration 2) and raising kp (iteration 3) both failed to move it. Every run still leaves the line at the 0.06 m off-track floor. The steady-bias and gain-tuning hypotheses are therefore exhausted.\n\nLikely cause: geometry. The sensors are 0.02 m apart at x = -0.04 to 0.04 with 0.012 m footprints, and the tape is 0.025 m wide. With the robot centred, only the x = 0 sensor sees tape. The outer sensors read zero until the robot is off-centre by about 0.0065 m, so the signal has a dead zone near the line and then jumps abruptly once an outer sensor starts reading. That gives a coarse, lagging steering response, which fits the slow drift to 0.06 m and the failure on every track. Nothing in the controller can fix a sensor layout that cannot see the line near the centre.\n\nChanges. (1) Sensor layout: move the five sensors to x = -0.016, -0.008, 0, 0.008, 0.016 at y = 0.04, and enlarge the footprint to sensor_size 0.016. Adjacent footprints now overlap across the tape, so the reading varies smoothly with lateral offset and the signal has no dead zone. (2) Controller gains return to the best raced values (kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.15), and base_speed stays at 1.3. This isolates the geometry change against iteration 1, the best raced design. Sensor weights stay [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2].\n\nExpected result. max_error should fall below about 0.055 m, line_loss_events should drop toward 0 on some seeds, and progress should rise on the oval and s-bend. If progress reaches about 0.995 with no line loss, raise base_speed toward 1.8.
